description: A few products and side projects I build to stay close to the craft.

projects.name: PLAYGRND
projects.description: A public amateur football record platform for leagues, matches, teams, players, claims, corrections, and organizer workflows.
highlights: SSR SvelteKit public app backed by a private Go API over local sockets
Postgres source-of-truth model with Redis snapshots and recomputable derived stats
WhatsApp magic-link onboarding, player claims, admin review, and scoped operational flows

caseStudy.intro: I am building PLAYGRND to give amateur footballers and organizers a credible public record: competitions, matches, teams, player profiles, honors, claims, and corrections in one fast, shareable product.
caseStudy.challenge: Local amateur football history exists, but it is fragmented across league sites, spreadsheets, social posts, and private organizer knowledge. The first job is not adding another social feed. It is turning that history into a trustworthy public record, then creating a controlled path for players and organizers to improve it.
productLoop: Publish fast, searchable league history with shareable player, team, match, and season pages.
Let players claim an existing profile through a channel they already use, without weakening identity checks.
Route claims and corrections through scoped admin review before they change the public record.
Use organizer workflows and real season feedback to decide what deserves to become native product functionality.

architecture.label: Public web
architecture.value: SvelteKit SSR with Croatian-first content and an English toggle

architecture.label: Application API
architecture.value: Private Go service reached over local sockets, with public writes kept behind the web layer

architecture.label: Source of truth
architecture.value: PostgreSQL for imported records, claims, identity, audit state, and deterministic aggregates

architecture.label: Hot reads
architecture.value: Redis snapshots for stable and short-lived public data, with PostgreSQL fallback

architecture.label: Identity and claims
architecture.value: WhatsApp magic links, short claim codes, pending profiles, and guarded approval flows

architecture.label: Operations
architecture.value: Hetzner releases, health checks, recompute tooling, backups, and documented rollback paths

decisions.title: Trust before creation
decisions.text: The product starts from explainable imported history. New write surfaces are added only when they close a real claim, correction, or organizer loop.

decisions.title: SSR-first public reads
decisions.text: Player and league pages should be fast, indexable, and useful when shared. The private API remains an implementation boundary rather than a public contract.

decisions.title: Recomputable derived data
decisions.text: Finished-season standings, scorers, and player statistics can be rebuilt transactionally from source records instead of becoming cache-shaped truth.

decisions.title: WhatsApp as a user channel
decisions.text: Login and claims meet local users in a familiar channel, while raw webhook storage, credentials, admin actions, and official record changes stay deliberately constrained.

delivered: Public league, match, team, player, standings, scorers, honors, search, and share flows
Croatian-first SSR product with responsive mobile search and profile discovery
WhatsApp magic-link login, pending-profile onboarding, profile claims, and admin review foundation
Persisted season aggregates, Redis hot-read snapshots, explicit recompute commands, and raw-data fallbacks
Operational tooling for deployment, health checks, backups, cache warming, derived-data audits, and rollback
caseStudy.next: The next proof is operational rather than cosmetic: harden real-phone claim flows, run the product with active competition organizers, and use that feedback to shape result entry, corrections, and recurring organizer workflows.

projects.name: Memoato
projects.description: A personal memory and quantified-self app for fast capture, life tracking, and long-term searchable history.
highlights: Fast capture with natural language input
Built for consistency, not spreadsheet rituals

caseStudy.intro: I am building Memoato as a low-friction personal memory system: capture a real-life note in natural language, preserve what was actually said, and turn the useful parts into structured history without forcing life into a spreadsheet first.
caseStudy.challenge: Most tracking tools make the user choose a category, form, unit, and exact structure before recording anything. That friction is especially expensive on busy days, which are often the days worth remembering. Memoato has to accept imperfect input quickly while keeping the raw record, derived facts, privacy choices, and later corrections understandable.
productLoop: Capture a short natural-language note from the web app, an MCP client, or another trusted integration.
Store the raw entry first, then extract structured facts with deterministic rules and a scoped AI fallback.
Match confident facts to existing categories, keep uncertain material visible, and avoid silently inventing history.
Turn accumulated entries into timelines, progress views, and useful recall without making dashboards the primary input model.

architecture.label: Product app
architecture.value: Wasp and React for authenticated capture, timelines, category views, and account workflows

architecture.label: Source of truth
architecture.value: PostgreSQL through Prisma for users, raw entries, structured events, categories, and timestamps

architecture.label: Ingestion
architecture.value: Raw-first API pipeline with deterministic parsing, optional model fallback, and asynchronous processing

architecture.label: Integrations
architecture.value: Revocable, hashed API keys scoped to raw-entry writes, plus a private MCP bridge

architecture.label: Privacy
architecture.value: Cloud, encrypted-cloud, and local-first product modes kept as explicit user choices

architecture.label: Operations
architecture.value: Hetzner deployment behind Caddy and systemd, with GitHub Actions release automation

decisions.title: Raw before derived
decisions.text: The original note is stored before parsing begins. Structured events can be corrected or rebuilt without erasing what the user actually recorded.

decisions.title: Confidence is a product concern
decisions.text: A plausible parse is not automatically a fact. Confident matches can become events; uncertain notes stay visible instead of being forced into the wrong category.

decisions.title: Categories are views
decisions.text: Goals, charts, and category pages remain useful, but capture starts with the user's words rather than requiring the user to navigate the data model.

decisions.title: Narrow integration access
decisions.text: MCP and automation tokens can write raw entries without receiving broad account access, and every key can be revoked or expired.

delivered: Natural-language quick logging with raw-entry preservation and asynchronous fact processing
Timeline, category, goal, chart, ordering, and human-readable daily summary views
Deterministic parsing plus optional AI-assisted extraction with unmatched notes retained
Scoped API keys and MCP ingestion for low-friction logging from trusted tools
Email and Google authentication, privacy modes, PWA support, and Hetzner production deployment
caseStudy.next: The next step is to make recall as useful as capture: improve correction flows, alias memory, provenance for derived facts, and summaries that help without pretending the system knows more than the underlying entries support.

projects.name: PLAYGRND Draft
projects.description: A fast football draft game where you spin iconic national-team tournament squads, build an XI, simulate a tournament, and share the result.
highlights: World XI draft loop built for quick mobile sessions
Local-first gameplay with non-blocking share and stats
Fan-made PLAYGRND experiment with careful rights boundaries

caseStudy.intro: I built PLAYGRND Draft as a fast football game for short mobile sessions: spin an iconic national-team tournament squad, draft an all-time XI by position, simulate the tournament, and share the result.
caseStudy.challenge: Football draft games are easy to overbuild. The core experience needs enough recognizable players and simulation depth to feel meaningful, but every login, network request, asset dependency, or long setup step makes a casual session less likely to finish. The product had to feel immediate while keeping sharing and aggregate learning available as optional layers.
productLoop: Generate a tournament squad capsule and present a position-specific choice from recognizable historical players.
Let the player complete a balanced XI without login, remote assets, or server-dependent game state.
Run a deterministic group and knockout simulation from the draft state and seed.
Offer a shareable result, then collect only anonymous aggregate signals without blocking gameplay.

architecture.label: Game client
architecture.value: Next.js, React, and TypeScript with drafting and simulation running locally in the browser

architecture.label: Football data
architecture.value: Curated tournament squads and independent ratings shipped with the application bundle

architecture.label: Simulation
architecture.value: Seeded, reproducible tournament runs covering group and knockout stages

architecture.label: Sharing
architecture.value: Compact saved runs behind short IDs, with local share text as the failure fallback

architecture.label: Aggregate stats
architecture.value: Optional Postgres-backed counters published as a static snapshot outside the gameplay path

architecture.label: Delivery
architecture.value: Static release directories on Hetzner behind Caddy, with the optional API managed separately

decisions.title: No backend in the game loop
decisions.text: Starting, drafting, simulating, and seeing a result must keep working if the share and stats API is unavailable.

decisions.title: Recognizable squads over exhaustive data
decisions.text: The first version favors iconic tournament capsules so most spins create an understandable football decision rather than a history quiz.

decisions.title: Deterministic by design
decisions.text: A seed and the selected XI are enough to reproduce a run, which keeps the simulation testable and makes compact sharing possible.

decisions.title: Rights-aware presentation
decisions.text: The fan-made game avoids official logos, player photos, trophy imagery, and claims of affiliation while keeping names and tournament facts descriptive.

delivered: Mobile-first positional draft flow built around curated historical tournament squads
Local deterministic tournament simulation with group and knockout progression
Shareable saved runs with graceful fallback when the optional API is unavailable
Anonymous aggregate statistics generated into a fast static public snapshot
Independent PLAYGRND branding, explicit rights boundaries, and Hetzner release deployment
caseStudy.next: The next useful work is learning from completed runs: tune squad variety and simulation balance, improve the moments people want to share, and add backend features only when they strengthen that loop without slowing it down.
